THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

These two appeals are filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 06.07.2011 in MVC.No.415/2009 passed by MACT-V, Court of Small Causes, Bangalore City, and judgment and award dated 22.07.2011 in MVC.No.248/2009 passed by Small Causes, Bangalore City (SCCH-12) contending that the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 is falsely implicated into the case.

sentences.text:
2. In MVC.No.415/2009, the facts are that, on 09.11.2008 at about 11.00 pm., petitioner was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing registration No. KA43.T.1517 on Bangalore-Devanahalli road,
during that time a driver of a lorry bearing registration No. KA.25.6268 came in a high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.
Due to impact of the said accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

In MVC.No.248/2009, the facts are that, on 09.11.2008 at about 11.00 pm.,
the victim in the said accident is Gowramma, aged 27 years, manager in private transport and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month met with an accident when he was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-43-J-1517 along with a pillion rider on left side on Banglaore-Devanahalli road, near MVT gate cross, Bangalore, at that time one lorry bearing No.KA-25-6268 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly dashed against the deceased vehicle and caused this accident.
Due to which the deceased pillion rider fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and he died on the spot.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 is falsely implicated into the case only NC: 2023:KHC:24860 for the purpose of making claim against the Insurance Company.

In the complaint, the number of lorry is not mentioned, but subsequently the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 without having any basis that this lorry was involved in the accident.

It is also submitted that from the evidence on record also as to how the Investigating Officer did come to know that this particular lorry was involved in the accident is not forthcoming from the evidence.
Therefore, it is submitted that lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 is falsely implicated into the case.

3 5.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1-claimants in both the cases submitted that after thorough investigation only, the Investigating Officer had filed the charge sheet and therefore, the statutory investigation carried out in this regard carries more weightage and significance.

Therefore, just because, there are some discrepancies in the evidence that does not go to core of the present case in proving that the lorry NC: 2023:KHC:24860 bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 is involved in the accident.
Hence, submitted that the offending lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 is involved in the accident and this is rightly considered by the Tribunals.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeals filed by the Insurance Company.

6. It is also submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.1-claimants in both the cases that in MVC.No.248/2009, the Tribunal has committed grave error in adopting multiplier of her old age mother and assessed the compensation.
But age of the deceased is to be considered for adopting the multiplier.
Therefore, submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in adopting multiplier of her old age mother resulting into erroneous judgment of granting compensation under the head loss of dependency.
Therefore, prays to modify the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
These are the fixed parameters as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others.
Vs. Delhi
Transport NC: 2023:KHC:24860 Corpn And Another 1 and National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2

sentences.text: . Therefore, prays for interference with the quantum of compensation awarded by exercising power under Order 41 Rule 33 of Code of Civil Procedure, even though, the claimants have not preferred appeal.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the appeals filed by the Insurance Company and prays for enhancement of quantum of compensation.

7. In the present case, it is alleged that the accident was caused on 09.11.2008 at night 11:00 p.m., as the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 had dashed the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-43-J-1517 from behind and due to which, the rider of the motor cycle succumbed to the injuries and pillion rider sustained injuries.
It is the contention of the Insurance Company that the lorry was falsely implicated into the case only for the purpose of claiming compensation.
When this being the contention, AIR 2009 SC 3104 (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC:24860 the evidence ought to be re-appreciated.

The First Information Statement which has been given by Ramesh has stated in the complaint that unknown lorry had dashed the motorcycle of the deceased and caused the accident,
but the registration number of the lorry is not mentioned.
Quite naturally, when the accident was caused on 09.11.2008 at night 11.00 pm., sometimes it could not be possible to note down the registration number of the vehicle.
The complaint was lodged on the very next day of the accident.
Hence, it cannot be said that there is much delay in lodging the complaint.

The MLC extract do not disclose as to what are the vehicles involved in the accident, but the wound certificate-Ex.R.2 in MVC.No.248/2009 shows that the alleged road traffic accident is because of involvement of the lorry, but the lorry number is not stated in the MLC register.

8. In this regard, upon appreciating the evidence of R.W.1-Investigating Officer who had conducted the investigation and upon pertinent question asked to the NC: 2023:KHC:24860 Investigating Officer as to how he came to know that such lorry has caused the accident, for this R.W.1-Investigating Officer has stated that Balaji and Narayan had given information about the registration number of the lorry.

Therefore, based upon the registration number given by these persons namely Balaji and Narayan, the Investigating Officer came to know the registration number The Manager Legal vs Smt Gowramma on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183033363/
4 of the lorry.

These persons namely Balaji and Narayan have been arraigned as charge sheeted witnesses No.4 and 5, so the Investigating Officer has made them as witnesses who have furnished the registration number of the lorry as charge sheeted witnesses.
One among them is Balaji who is examined as P.W.2.

It is the evidence of P.W.2 that he was standing near the place of accident for the purposes of bringing tea and at that time, the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 coming with high speed dashed against the motor cycle and due to which, the deceased died and others sustained injuries.

Therefore, upon considering the case on all its preponderance of probabilities initially in the complaint at an undisputed point of time, it is stated in the complaint that the lorry had dashed the motorcycle.
Since, the accident was caused at night 11.00 pm., quite naturally, it could not be possible to note down the lorry number.
Therefore, the nature and class of vehicle involved in the accident is proved as it is a lorry.
Whether this lorry is involved in the accident or not, then the evidence of the Investigation Officer and Balaji ought to be considered.
The Investigation Officer had stated that Balaji and Narayan had furnished the registration number of the lorry.
This exercise is during the course of investigation and cannot be found unnatural one.
Moreover, the said Balaji had given evidence before the Tribunal that he had seen the accident and lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 had caused the accident.
During the course of cross- examination, nothing is revealed so as to affect the core of the case that this lorry was not involved in the accident.

Therefore, upon considering all these evidence on record and on its preponderance of probabilities, it is proved that the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 had dashed the motorcycle and caused the accident.

There may be some minor discrepancies regarding place of accident given by the witnesses, but that does not affect the core of the claim as the case is in the nature of claim proceeding and appreciation of evidence cannot be done by applying principle beyond reasonable doubt, which has to be done in the criminal case, but by applying principle of preponderance of probabilities.
Therefore, upon considering the evidence on record on all its preponderance of probabilities as discussed above, it is proved that the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25-6268 has caused the accident.
Based on this investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed the charge sheet against the driver by mentioning that the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-25- 6268 is involved in the accident.
Therefore, in this regard, the appeals filed by the Insurance Company are liable to be dismissed.

- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:24860 Regarding quantum of compensation:

Even though, the claimant has not filed appeal for enhancement of compensation, but considering that there is flagrant error committed by the Tribunal in assessing the quantum of compensation, resulting into miscarriage of justice, as the Tribunal has adopted the multiplier according to the age of the claimant who is the mother of the deceased, but the multiplier ought to have been adopted as per the age of the deceased on the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Smt.Sarla Verma and Pranay Sethi.

Therefore, this Court by exercising its power under Order 41 Rule 33 of CPC rectifies the quantum of compensation in the interest of justice, otherwise, it would be perpetrating miscarriage of justice.

Therefore, for this purpose, this Court is exercising its power for re-determining the compensation only insofar as death of the deceased is concerned.
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:24860 12.
As per the post mortem report of the deceased the age of the deceased is 27 years.

Admittedly,
the deceased is a bachelor.
The claimant is the mother of the deceased alone.
The multiplier is to be taken as per the age of the deceased.

As per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Smt.Sarla Verma and Pranay Sethi, the claimant is an old age mother of the deceased alone who has lost her son at the young age and therefore, she might not have filed appeal before the Appellate Court for seeking enhancement of compensation.
But just because, the appeal is not filed for enhancement that alone is not a ground to consider the case for enhancement.

13. Therefore, in order to rectify the miscarriage of justice committed by the Tribunal, the amount of compensation is to be re-determined in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in catena of decisions.

The deceased was aged 27 years old and working as a manager in the private transport office and - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:24860 was claiming to be drawing salary of Rs.10,000/- pm., but there is no evidence to prove the income of the deceased in this regard.

Therefore, on this basis, the notional income ought to be taken as Rs.4,500/- pm., since the accident is of the year 2008 as per the Notional Income Chart recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
40% of income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case.
As the deceased was aged 27 years as on the date of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable is 17.
Since the deceased is a bachelor, 50% of income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

Hence,
compensation under the head loss of dependency is re-assessed and quantified as follows:
Rs.4,500/- + Rs.1,800/- (40% of Rs.4,500/-)=Rs.6,300/- Rs.6,300/- x 50% x 17 x 12=Rs.6,42,600/-
The Manager Legal vs Smt Gowramma on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183033363/
6
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.6,42,600/- is awarded under the head loss of dependency.
Further compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head loss of estate as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
15. Further compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head transportation, funeral and obsequies as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of love and affection.
The loss of love and affection and loss of consortium are having the same connotation.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v.
Nanu Ram & Others3, each legal dependents are entitled for Rs.40,000/-.

Bangalore City, is hereby confirmed.
